names.official: Personal income tax (PIT), State share
names.native: Podatek dochodowy od osób fizycznych (część państwa)

taxes.base: Employment income (PLN 85.2 billion), self-employment (58.8 billion), social benefits (28.3 billion), capital gains (9.0 billion) and the solidarity contribution (2.1 billion).
taxes.payer: Individuals; employers and payers withhold it.

rate.headline: 12% · 32% above PLN 120,000
details: 12% of the base less a deduction of PLN 3,600 (tax-free amount PLN 30,000) up to PLN 120,000, then PLN 10,800 plus 32% of the excess (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 11 August 2026), not checked against the National Revenue Administration.

instruments.explanation: The National Tax List gives one total for the personal income tax (PLN 183.5 billion); Eurostat’s accounts place PLN 101.8 billion of it with local government and the rest with the State. This row is the State’s part, the next the local governments’.

names.official: Corporate income tax (CIT), State share
names.native: Podatek dochodowy od osób prawnych (część państwa)

taxes.base: Profit of companies and other legal persons.

rate.headline: 19% standard; 9% for small taxpayers
details: The standard CIT rate is 19% and a reduced 9% applies to small taxpayers; from 2026 banks pay 23% (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 11 August 2026), not checked against the National Revenue Administration.

instruments.explanation: The National Tax List gives one total for the corporate income tax (PLN 87.5 billion); Eurostat places PLN 26.5 billion with local government and the rest with the State.
